stem.en: Can you close ___ door, please? It's cold.

why.en: Both speakers know which door (the one in this room), so we use the.
why.uz: Ikkala suhbatdosh qaysi eshik ekanini biladi (shu xonadagi), shuning uchun the.
why.ru: Оба собеседника знают, о какой двери речь (в этой комнате), поэтому the.

why.uz: Umuman musiqa haqida gapirilyapti, shuning uchun artikl ishlatilmaydi.
why.ru: Речь о музыке вообще, поэтому артикль не нужен.

stem.en: We usually go to school by ___ bus.

why.en: With by + transport (by bus, by car, by train) there is no article.
why.uz: By + transport birikmasida (by bus, by car, by train) artikl ishlatilmaydi.
why.ru: В сочетании by + транспорт (by bus, by car, by train) артикль не ставится.

stem.en: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.

why.en: In the first conditional, the if-part uses the present simple (rains), not will.
why.uz: Birinchi tur shart gapda if qismi Present Simple da boʻladi (rains), will ishlatilmaydi.
why.ru: В условных предложениях первого типа в части с if — Present Simple (rains), а не will.

stem.en: If you study hard, you ___ the exam.

why.en: The result part of the first conditional uses will + the base verb: will pass.
why.uz: Birinchi tur shart gapning natija qismi will + feʼlning asosiy shakli: will pass.
why.ru: Часть-результат в условных первого типа: will + начальная форма: will pass.

stem.en: If I see Malika, I ___ her your message.

why.en: If + present simple, then will + the base verb: I will give.
why.uz: If + Present Simple, keyin will + feʼlning asosiy shakli: I will give.
why.ru: If + Present Simple, затем will + начальная форма: I will give.

options.en: If it's sunny, we'll go out.
If it will be sunny, we'll go out.
If it was sunny, we'll go out.
If it's sunny, we'd go out.

why.en: First conditional: if + present simple (it's sunny), will in the other part (we'll go out).
why.uz: Birinchi tur shart gap: if + Present Simple (it's sunny), ikkinchi qismda will (we'll go out).
why.ru: Условное первого типа: if + Present Simple (it's sunny), в другой части will (we'll go out).

stem.en: This is the book ___ I told you about.

why.en: For things we use that or which; who is for people, and what cannot follow a noun.
why.uz: Narsalar uchun that yoki which; who odamlar uchun, what esa otdan keyin kelmaydi.
why.ru: Для предметов — that или which; who — для людей, а what не ставится после существительного.

stem.en: A nurse is a person ___ looks after sick people.

why.en: Person is a human, so the relative pronoun is who.
why.uz: Person — inson, shuning uchun nisbiy olmosh who.
why.ru: Person — человек, поэтому относительное местоимение who.

stem.en: That's the hospital ___ I was born.

why.en: For a place where something happens we use where: the hospital where I was born.
why.uz: Biror narsa sodir boʻlgan joy uchun where: the hospital where I was born.
why.ru: Для места, где что-то происходит, используется where: the hospital where I was born.

options.en: The man which lives here is a doctor.
The bag that I lost was red.
She's the girl who won the prize.
I like films which make me laugh.

why.en: For people we use who or that, not which: the man who lives here.
why.uz: Odamlar uchun which emas, who yoki that: the man who lives here.
why.ru: Для людей используется who или that, а не which: the man who lives here.

stem.en: The film was so ___ that I fell asleep.

why.en: An -ing adjective describes the thing that causes the feeling: the film was boring.
why.uz: -ing bilan tugaydigan sifat his-tuygʻuga sabab boʻlgan narsani tasvirlaydi: the film was boring.
why.ru: Прилагательное на -ing описывает то, что вызывает чувство: the film was boring.

stem.en: I'm ___ in history. I read a lot about it.

why.en: An -ed adjective describes how a person feels: I'm interested in history.
why.uz: -ed bilan tugaydigan sifat insonning his-tuygʻusini bildiradi: I'm interested in history.
why.ru: Прилагательное на -ed описывает чувства человека: I'm interested in history.

stem.en: We were very ___ when we heard the good news.

why.en: The sentence describes how people (we) felt, so we use the -ed adjective: excited.
why.uz: Gap odamlarning (we) his-tuygʻusini tasvirlaydi, shuning uchun -ed sifati: excited.
why.ru: Предложение описывает чувства людей (we), поэтому прилагательное на -ed: excited.

stem.en: The journey was long and ___, so we went to bed early.

why.en: The journey caused the feeling, so it was tiring; people feel tired.
why.uz: Sayohat charchoqqa sabab boʻldi, shuning uchun tiring; odamlar esa tired boʻladi.
why.ru: Поездка вызвала усталость, поэтому tiring; а люди бывают tired.
